records.region: Northeastern Alaska; Aichilik and Egaksrak coastal corridors
records.material_pending_reason: The selected eastward traverse across the coastal wetland plain from the Aichilik braid belt to Egaksrak River lacks an independently depicted lateral channel or connected waterbody passage. Upstream and downstream named components are individually supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Aichilik River identifies the long upper, middle and lower-plain approach. Egaksrak River identifies the final river and delta approach. The unresolved intervening lateral traverse prevents a supported whole-selected-system identity.
records.completion_scope: All twenty parts and the single fragment were considered against three successfully acquired original cartographic views. Chosen opening, upper and middle valley, lower Aichilik approach, final Egaksrak delta and actual terminal have ordinary source correspondence. Parts 16–18 lack the selected Aichilik-to-Egaksrak lateral through-link. This is one material-pending finding rather than completed identity, completed scope hold or a second access-pending status.
records.supported_name_scope: Direct cartographic labels support the two named components within their actual observed reaches. Different reach names can coexist in a representative system, but they do not prove an otherwise unestablished connection.

scope_limits: Minor valley-side offsets and simplified headward bends are accepted at ordinary corridor scale and are not separately classified as material gaps.
No present flow direction, active seasonal distributary, exact natural spring/source, exact shoreline or formal hydronym boundary is established.
Upslope glacial/snow depiction is geographic context only; no through-glacier hydraulic claim is made.
The shared delta/lagoon destination and two supported component names do not establish the missing lateral connection.

bounded_name_observations.role: Mapped selected opening, mountain/middle route and lower-plain approach.

bounded_name_observations.role: Mapped final river/delta component, with the intervening selected lateral connection still pending.

records.material_pending_reason: The eastern chosen feeder and its join into lower Piura, the selected Las Salinas-to-eastern-Virrilá connection, and the actual final shore crossing toward Bahía de Sechura remain unestablished. The expedition southern Zapayal route and Parachique mouth are not substituted for the selection.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The independently documented lower Piura river–lake corridor reaching the Virrilá setting. The candidate is not established as the representative identity of the entire selected feature because the eastern feeder, a chosen estuary-entry connector and the actual stored terminal remain unresolved.
records.completion_scope: All 27 selected parts were considered. Documented lower Piura, Ramón and Salinas waterbody passages and the internal Virrilá estuary have bounded support; the specific eastern feeder, chosen estuary entry and stored coastal terminal remain materially incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: The independently documented lower Piura river–lake corridor reaching the Virrilá setting. The candidate is not established as the representative identity of the entire selected feature because the eastern feeder, a chosen estuary-entry connector and the actual stored terminal remain unresolved.

scope_limits: The eastern opening name and river/canal status remain unestablished.
The selected entry into Virrilá is not necessarily the expedition’s documented southern route.
The stored terminal cannot be replaced by a nearby mouth or by the field expedition endpoint.
Historical observations establish source depiction for their dates, not present flow, current structures or operating status.

records.material_pending_reason: The actual southern feeder, central western foothill links, approach into the delta network and complete selected final passage into Shallow Bay are not established by the inspected community, land-use and coastal sources.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The community conservation plan identifies the Big Fish River watershed in the selected western Mackenzie Delta foothill setting. This remains a provisional candidate for the inland corridor, not a completed whole-system representative identification. The selected downstream delta channels and bay extension must not be assigned the same scalar name.
records.completion_scope: All 22 selected parts were considered. Big Fish watershed and lower-delta/Shallow Bay context are documented, but the chosen opening, intermediate route, delta join and final selected bay connection remain materially incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: The community conservation plan identifies the Big Fish River watershed in the selected western Mackenzie Delta foothill setting. This remains a provisional candidate for the inland corridor, not a completed whole-system representative identification. The selected downstream delta channels and bay extension must not be assigned the same scalar name.

scope_limits: Big Fish River is a provisional watershed candidate, not a verified representative name for every selected component.
Distinct inland and delta reach names could coexist; unresolved correspondence, rather than name uniformity, prevents completion.
No exact banks, present flow conditions, current operations, island-side channel precision or formal name-boundary vertices were required or claimed.
No code, tests, application records, geometry, shared public totals, repository branches or portable packages were changed.

records.region: Seward–Malaspina glaciated border corridor and Malaspina Lake coastal outlet, Yakutat region
records.material_pending_reason: The lower mainstem crosses a ridged, pond-rich foreland between the eastern Malaspina ice margin and the first continuously mapped stream into Malaspina Lake. Neither the independent reference maps nor the regional SAR imagery establishes this selected through-connection; the upper glacier, both lake tributary stages and actual coastal outlet are otherwise geographically accounted for.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected object combines a long ice corridor, a materially unestablished foreland through-link, a lake-crossing tributary and a short coastal outlet. No single natural-river or representative-system name is established.
records.completion_scope: All five fragments have source-linked observations. Geographic correspondence is complete for the chosen Canadian ice opening, middle glacier corridor, both selected lake tributary stages, downstream lake approach/junction and coastal terminal. A specific foreland through-connection in lower mainstem FID2737 remains unestablished. Therefore this is one material-pending record, not a completed naming-scope hold and not an additional access-pending record.
records.supported_name_scope: The selected object combines a long ice corridor, a materially unestablished foreland through-link, a lake-crossing tributary and a short coastal outlet. No single natural-river or representative-system name is established.

scope_limits: Geographic ice-corridor correspondence is not proof of a natural surface river, subglacial hydraulic path or single river name.
No current glacier-margin survey, exact channel bank, tidal boundary or contemporary flow state is claimed.
The SAR paper’s colored flow lines are model-derived approximations and were not treated as measured watercourses.
The short coastal outlet names are kept within their directly depicted local scope; no whole-system identity or official naming-registry verification is claimed.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
